title: Progressive annotation layer with keyboard-first tooltips for high-density time-series
creator: Elena Moroz
description: Design and prototype a progressive annotation/overlay layer for dense time-series charts that defers heavy rendering until needed, provides keyboard-first tooltip interactions, and preserves WCAG contrast and screen-reader semantics. Goal is measurable CPU reduction at render time for dashboards with many series while improving discoverability for keyboard and assistive users.
acceptance_criteria: A11y: All tooltip content must be reachable via keyboard tabbing and exposed to screen readers with appropriate ARIA roles
Performance: Initial page render CPU usage for a 50-series dashboard should be reduced by at least 30% compared to current baseline
Progressive rendering: Annotation layer should use placeholder skeletons and lazy hydrate detailed rendering on hover/focus or viewport intersection
Design tokens: Colors, spacing and microinteraction durations must be expressed via design tokens to support theming and dark-mode contrast testing
Edge cases: Tooltips support simultaneous pointer + keyboard focus without duplicate announcements or focus traps
design_notes: Introduce an 'annotation layer' composited above existing chart canvas so visual series rendering remains GPU-accelerated while annotations/tooltips are DOM-managed for a11y
Create two tooltip modes: lightweight summary bubbles for pointer hover (low-cost) and expanded keyboard-mode panels that include semantic headings, actionable links and copyable timestamps
Use IntersectionObserver to delay heavy SVG/text layout until annotations enter viewport; use requestIdleCallback for non-critical hydrations on supported browsers
Tokenize tooltip spacing, typographic scale, and color semantics as token variables: token-tooltip-bg, token-tooltip-border, token-focus-ring, token-annotation-gap
Design fallback for low-powered devices: disable expanded keyboard panel and show simplified aria-live updates when CPU budget is low (configurable via runtime flag)
Prototype interaction sequences in Figma using both pointer-first and keyboard-first flows to validate motion and focus order
accessibility_considerations: Keyboard focus order must follow logical reading order: chart series legend -> series focus -> annotation tooltip -> close/next action
Tooltips must use role='dialog' only for expanded keyboard panels; hover summaries should use role='status' with aria-live='polite' to avoid spamming SRs
Maintain minimum 4.5:1 contrast for tooltip foreground/background in light and dark themes; verify with tokenized color pairs
Avoid relying solely on color to convey series identity; include shape/label in tooltip header
Test with VoiceOver and NVDA using sample datasets and with high-density charts where tooltips may queue
performance_tuning_plan: Measure baseline using internal perf dashboard with 5, 20, 50 series payloads; capture CPU, main-thread work, and first-frame render
Implement progressive hydration: lightweight DOM with minimal text on first paint, defer heavy layout to user interaction or idle time
Batch tooltip updates during rapid pointer movement using 80ms coalescing window to reduce reflows
Introduce 'annotation cache' keyed by series+time-range to reuse layout for repeated opens
Coordinate with ENG-2041 to add a runtime flag that opts charts into lazy annotation rendering; provide telemetry for adoption and perf impact
tradeoffs: Using a DOM-based annotation layer improves a11y but may complicate pixel-perfect overlays with GPU canvas — we'll accept minor alignment variances in favor of semantic markup
Deferring rendering reduces initial CPU but increases perceived latency on first tooltip open; mitigated by skeletons and prefetch heuristics for focused charts
Role='dialog' for keyboard-expanded panels gives richer semantics but risks SR verbosity; we will limit announcements and provide concise headings
decisions: Primary decision: implement a separate DOM annotation layer above canvas rather than rendering annotations into canvas
Adopt token names prefixed with token-tooltip-* and token-annotation-* for consistency with design system
Keyboard-expanded tooltip will be a focusable panel with an explicit close button and optional action list
Fallback mode enabled for low-power devices and when runtime flag is disabled
